acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Boars family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Old Tusk, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Stampede Sovereign archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Enormous ancient boar with one broken outer tusk, root-tangled mane, layered shoulder scars, and an extremely low unstoppable silhouette.
Signature mechanic: Three-Lane Stampede: each tusk scores a lane and assigns Bristle Hogs, Tunnel Boars, or Razorbacks to lead it before Old Tusk takes the final gap.
battlefieldDuty: Create three successive stampede lanes before personally collapsing the remaining safe route.
constructionDimensions: Packed soil and mineral plates reinforce the forehead, shoulders, hooves, and tusk bases while hide and bristles remain dominant.
Charges peel up coherent furrows and detached stones that follow the exact route.
counterplay: Interrupt a lane leader to preserve its gap, then redirect Old Tusk into the disabled route's obstacle. Affinity signal: A pale fracture seam opens at the planted hoof or outside shoulder when the Boar commits to turning or bracing.
forbiddenTreatments: Random floating rocks unrelated to the charge route
identityInvariants: Every form keeps a low four-legged boar body, cloven hooves, mobile snout, raised bristles, short tail, and visible tusk roots.
Tier escalation uses tusk geometry, neck mass, shoulder callus, scars, and bristle profile rather than humanoid equipment.
Charge direction remains readable through hoof placement, lowered head angle, tusk contact, dust, and the alignment of the spine.
telegraph: The mane rises from tail to skull and the assigned lane leader stamps once inside its scored route.
